headline: ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund launches new contra fund for subscription
hook: New fund targets out-of-favour market sectors
summary: ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund has opened its new Contra Fund for public subscription until October 12. The scheme employs a contrarian investment strategy, targeting out-of-favour companies with potential for operational turnaround. Fund experts emphasize that this approach demands deep research, high patience, and an extended investment horizon. Retail investors should note that contrarian funds can suffer prolonged periods of underperformance while waiting for market sentiment to shift.
why_it_matters: Contrarian funds demand high patience through prolonged underperformance phases.

headline: Top and bottom performing midcap mutual funds
hook: Midcap SIP performance gap widens significantly
summary: HSBC Midcap Fund led the category with a 17.5% SIP return over the last two years. WhiteOak and ICICI Prudential also ranked among the top performers, while the category average stood at 7.85%. Monthly SIP flows into the midcap segment have increased by 37%. Retail investors should compare fund-specific performance against category averages to assess their portfolio health.
why_it_matters: Review your midcap fund's performance against category benchmarks.
winners_losers: HSBC Midcap holders gain / Laggard fund holders hurt

headline: ICICI Prudential 10-year Constant Maturity Gilt Fund performance overview
hook: Performance update for ICICI Prudential Gilt fund
summary: The ICICI Prudential 10-year Constant Maturity Gilt Fund Direct-Growth plan invests primarily in government securities with a 10-year maturity profile. These funds are sensitive to interest rate fluctuations and are typically used by investors seeking sovereign-backed credit quality. The fund's performance is tied to the yield movements of long-term government bonds. Retail investors often use such funds to hedge against equity market volatility or to take a view on interest rate cycles.
why_it_matters: Long-term bond yields directly impact your debt fund returns.
